title: Morning vs Evening Mood Gap
dataSources: Mood entries (`mood:entry`), meditation sessions (`meditation:session`), journal entries (`journal:entry`), gratitude logs (`gratitude:log`).
app: Mood, mindfulness and journaling apps — Daylio / How We Feel mood exports, Headspace / Insight Timer meditation logs, journaling and gratitude entries — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=mood:entry
| eval daypart=if(tonumber(strftime(_time,"%H"))<12,"morning","evening")
| stats avg(mood_score) as avg_mood, count as entries by daypart
| eventstats avg(avg_mood) as overall
| eval delta_from_overall=round(avg_mood-overall,2)
description: Compares whether you usually feel stronger in the morning or the evening.
value: Knowing when your mood is naturally better helps you place demanding work, reflection, or social time in the right part of the day.
implementation: Collect timestamped mood scores in `index=personal`; compare averages between morning and evening entries.
visualization: Two-bar comparison of average morning and evening mood.
grandmaExplanation: It logs whether mornings or evenings are usually better for you, which helps you plan harder tasks for the right time.
